criteria.description: The up migration runs without error on a Postgres database containing an existing users table with an email column.

criteria.verification: Query information_schema.columns for users.deleted_at. Confirm data_type is 'timestamp without time zone' or 'timestamp with time zone', is_nullable = 'YES', and column_default IS NULL.

criteria.description: The migration does not write any values to existing rows: deleted_at is NULL for every pre-existing row and no other column values change.
criteria.verification: Snapshot the users rows before migrating. After the up migration, confirm every row has deleted_at IS NULL and all other column values match the snapshot. Also confirm the migration SQL contains no UPDATE or INSERT statement on users.

criteria.description: The up migration creates an index on users(email) whose predicate is deleted_at IS NULL.
criteria.verification: Query pg_indexes or pg_index for users. Confirm exactly one new index exists whose key column is email and whose predicate (pg_get_expr(indpred)) is equivalent to (deleted_at IS NULL).

criteria.description: After a run, the S3 bucket/prefix holds the 14 newest backups and deletes older ones; backups outside the script's prefix are not touched.

criteria.description: The script exits with a non-zero status when any step fails: database dump failure, S3 upload failure, or retention cleanup failure.
criteria.verification: In the sandbox, run three times injecting one failure each time: bad DB credentials or unreachable host, an unwritable or nonexistent bucket, and an S3 deny on list/delete. criteria.description: The script exits with status 0 when the dump, upload, and retention all succeed.
criteria.verification: Run the script in the working sandbox configuration; pass if exit code is 0.

criteria.description: A failed or partial dump is not uploaded and does not count toward the 14 retained backups.
criteria.verification: Inject a pg_dump failure mid-run in the sandbox; pass if no new object appears in S3 and no existing backups are deleted.

criteria.description: The deliverable is a single well-formed CSV file that parses without errors, with a header row and the same number of fields in every row.

criteria.description: Each output phone number represents the same number as the source row's phone, with only formatting and country-code prefixing changed.

criteria.description: The deliverable is a single valid CSV file with a header row containing exactly the columns date, description, amount, balance, in that order.
criteria.verification: Parse the file with a standard CSV parser; confirm it parses without error, there is exactly one file, and the header row equals [date, description, amount, balance].

criteria.description: The CSV contains transactions from every one of the 12 provided statements, with no statement period omitted.
criteria.verification: For each provided statement, confirm at least one CSV row falls within that statement's period (or the statement shows no transactions) and that dates span the full 12-month range.

criteria.description: The number of CSV transaction rows for each statement equals the number of transaction lines on that statement, with no transactions missing or duplicated.
criteria.verification: Extract transaction lines from each source PDF and compare the per-statement count to the CSV rows in that period; any mismatch fails.

criteria.description: For each statement, the opening balance plus the sum of CSV amounts in that period equals the statement's closing balance to the cent.
criteria.verification: For each statement, take its printed opening and closing balances and confirm opening + sum(CSV amounts for that period) = closing exactly (difference of 0.00).

criteria.description: Each row's balance equals the previous row's balance plus the current row's amount, to the cent.
criteria.verification: Iterate rows in file order; for each row after the first, confirm balance = previous balance + amount with zero difference. Rows sharing a date are checked in statement order.

criteria.description: Each row's date, amount, and balance match the corresponding transaction line on the source statement.
criteria.verification: Align CSV rows to extracted PDF transaction lines (all rows, or a random sample of at least 50 rows spread across all 12 statements); any mismatch in date, amount, or balance fails.

criteria.description: Amounts are signed so that debits/withdrawals are negative and credits/deposits are positive.

criteria.description: Each row's description reproduces the transaction description text from the statement, without truncation of multi-line descriptions.

request: Transcribe the attached 45-minute podcast episode and add speaker labels and timestamps every 30 seconds.

output.title: Transcribe 45-minute podcast with speaker labels and 30-second timestamps

criteria.description: The transcript covers the entire episode from start to end, with no unexplained untranscribed stretches longer than 30 seconds that contain speech.
criteria.verification: Compare the audio duration with the transcript's last timestamp, which must fall within 30 seconds of the end of the audio. Run speech activity detection on the audio and confirm every 30-second window containing speech has transcribed text or an explicit [inaudible]/[crosstalk] marker.

criteria.description: A timestamp in a consistent HH:MM:SS (or MM:SS) format appears at every 30-second interval, starting at 00:00:00 and continuing through the end of the audio.
criteria.verification: Parse all timestamps. Pass only if the first is 00:00:00 or 00:00, every consecutive pair differs by exactly 30 seconds, all use one consistent format, and the count equals floor(audio duration / 30) + 1, with no missing or duplicate markers.

criteria.description: Each timestamp is placed at the point in the text that corresponds to that moment in the audio, within ±5 seconds.
criteria.verification: Force-align the transcript text to the audio. For every timestamp marker, compare the audio time of the adjacent word with the marker value. Pass if every marker is within 5 seconds.

criteria.description: Every speaker turn begins with a speaker label, and each speaker uses one consistent label throughout.
criteria.verification: Pass only if every paragraph or turn of spoken text is preceded by a label such as 'Name:' or 'Speaker 1:', and the number of distinct labels matches the number of distinct speakers found by diarization of the audio, with no variant spellings of the same speaker.

criteria.description: Speech is attributed to the correct speaker for at least 95% of turns.
criteria.verification: Run speaker diarization on the audio, align it with the transcript turns, and compute the share of turns whose label matches the diarized speaker. Pass if it is 95% or higher.

criteria.description: The transcript has a word error rate of 5% or lower against the audio.
criteria.verification: Sample at least five 2-minute segments spread across the episode, produce reference transcripts (by human review or a high-accuracy ASR reference with human adjudication), and compute word error rate after normalizing case and punctuation. Pass if the aggregate WER is 5% or lower.

criteria.description: The transcript is in the language spoken in the audio and contains no summaries, paraphrased sections, or added commentary beyond speaker labels, timestamps, and bracketed non-speech markers.
criteria.verification: Check that the transcript language matches the audio language. Confirm that all text outside labels, timestamps, and bracketed markers aligns to spoken audio, and that no paragraph is a summary or editorial note.

criteria.description: Unintelligible or overlapping speech is marked with a bracketed tag such as [inaudible] or [crosstalk], with a timestamp, rather than being guessed or silently omitted.
criteria.verification: Review audio regions flagged as low-confidence by ASR or alignment. Pass if each region is either transcribed accurately or marked with a bracketed tag that includes a timestamp.

open_questions: Should speakers be labeled by real name (requires the buyer to provide names) or generically (Host, Guest 1 / Speaker 1, Speaker 2)?
Do you want a verbatim transcript (including ums, false starts, and repetitions) or a clean-verbatim transcript with fillers removed? This changes how accuracy is measured.
What file format should the deliverable use: plain text, DOCX, SRT/VTT, or another?
Is the 5% word error rate threshold acceptable, or do you need higher accuracy, for example for publication?
Should 30-second timestamps be inserted exactly at the time mark, even mid-sentence, or at the nearest sentence boundary? This affects the alignment tolerance.

criteria.description: Edits are limited to grammar, spelling, and punctuation; no tracked change alters meaning, adds or removes claims, rewrites sentences for style, or changes numbers, data, names, or technical terms.
criteria.verification: Judge reviews every tracked revision and fails the criterion if any single revision changes meaning, adds or removes an idea, restructures a sentence beyond what a grammatical fix requires, or alters a number, proper name, quotation, or domain term.

criteria.description: After all revisions are accepted, the chapter contains no unambiguous spelling errors in ordinary words.

request: Write the copy for a 5-email welcome sequence for our fintech app, one email every 2 days. Each email needs a subject line under 50 characters and a single CTA.

output.title: 5-email welcome sequence copy for a fintech app

criteria.description: The deliverable contains exactly 5 distinct emails, clearly separated and numbered or labeled in send order.
criteria.verification: Count the distinct emails in the deliverable; pass if exactly 5, each identifiable as a separate email with a position in the sequence.

criteria.description: Each of the 5 emails has exactly one labeled subject line.
criteria.verification: For each email, confirm a single subject line is present and identifiable (e.g., labeled 'Subject:'). Fail if any email lacks one or has multiple unlabeled alternatives without a designated final choice.

criteria.description: Every subject line is under 50 characters (49 or fewer), counting spaces, punctuation, and emoji.
criteria.verification: Measure the character length of each designated subject line; pass only if all 5 are 49 characters or fewer.

criteria.description: Each email contains exactly one call to action, meaning one distinct action the reader is asked to take, which may be repeated as the same link or button but not combined with a different action.
criteria.verification: For each email, identify all requests for the reader to take an action, such as links, buttons, or imperative prompts to do something. Pass if each email asks for exactly one distinct action. Fail if an email has none or asks for two or more different actions. Standard footer elements such as unsubscribe links do not count.

criteria.description: The sequence indicates send timing of one email every 2 days, with Email 1 on day 0 and Emails 2–5 on days 2, 4, 6, and 8, or an equivalent 2-day spacing.
criteria.verification: Check that each email is labeled with a send day or delay and that consecutive emails are spaced exactly 2 days apart.

criteria.description: Each email includes complete body copy, with no placeholder text such as 'lorem ipsum', '[insert copy]', or 'TBD' standing in for the message.
criteria.verification: Search each email for body text and for placeholder markers (lorem ipsum, TBD, TODO, [insert...]). Bracketed personalization tokens such as {first_name} or [App Name] are allowed. Fail if any email lacks body copy or uses a placeholder in place of content.

criteria.description: The copy is written as an onboarding/welcome sequence for a new user of a fintech app, with each email advancing onboarding rather than repeating the same message.
criteria.verification: Judge reads all 5 emails and passes if (a) Email 1 welcomes a new user, (b) the content refers to a financial or money app context, and (c) no two emails have substantially the same purpose and CTA.

criteria.description: The copy makes no guaranteed-return, risk-free, or specific numeric financial performance claims (e.g., interest rates, fee amounts, returns) unless those figures were provided by the buyer.
criteria.verification: Scan for phrases like 'guaranteed', 'risk-free', or 'no risk', and for specific rates, percentages, or fee figures. Fail if any appear without a buyer-provided source.

open_questions: What is the app's name, product (e.g., banking, investing, budgeting, payments), and target audience? Without these, the seller may use placeholders like [App Name].
What should the CTAs drive, for example completing KYC, linking a bank account, making a first deposit, or enabling notifications? Should specific actions be assigned to specific emails?
Is preheader/preview text also required for each email?
Is there a desired body length per email, a brand voice or tone guide, or required compliance or disclaimer language?
What delivery format do you want: plain text, Google Doc, or HTML-ready copy?
